## Project Overview

This notebook prep  ares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** Child and Adolescent Trauma Screen (CATS) assessment data for analysis and reporting (SQ 3.15, PTSD). It ingests three raw eInsight exports, processes the two-row hierarchical headers, maps text responses to numeric values, computes symptom totals, severity bands and cutoff flags, pairs each client's initial assessment with their last follow-up, and writes one clean paired output per version.

**Data sources (eInsight Individual Assessments exports; file names set in Setup):**

-   **CATS-2 self-report, 7–17 years** and **CATS-2 caregiver report, 7–17 years** (version 2.0, Sachser et al., 2022).
-   **CATS caregiver report, 3–6 years** (original CATS).

**Scoring** follows the scoring pages printed on each form:

-   Only the symptom items are scored. They are found by their answers: the `_response` columns where most answers are on the form's frequency scale. The trauma-event and functional-impairment questions (Yes/No) and the free-text questions drop out.
-   **CATS-2, 7–17 (both versions):** 25 symptom rows rated Never = 0, Sometimes = 1, Often = 2, Almost always = 3, in form order (1–8, 9a–9d, 10a–10b, 11–14, 15a–15b, 16–20). Items 9, 10 and 15 count only their highest sub-item, giving 20 items. DSM-5 PTSD sum range 0–60. Bands: Normal (<15), Moderate (15–20), Elevated (21–24; positive screen at ≥21), Probable PTSD (≥25).
-   **CATS, 3–6:** 16 symptom items rated Never = 0, Once in a while = 1, Half the time = 2, Almost always = 3. Total range 0–48. 12 or above is clinical.
-   Higher scores indicate more trauma-related distress. **A lower follow-up score indicates a positive outcome.**
-   **Missing items** (project default, D10; the forms give no rule): up to 10% of items may be blank (2 of 20 for 7–17; 1 of 16 for 3–6), and the total is prorated (sum of answered items × number of items ÷ number answered, rounded). A split item (9, 10, 15) is blank only when all its sub-items are blank.

**Pairing logic:** Clients are grouped by `client_system_id`. The first assessment is the initial; the last assessment (if ≥2 exist) is the follow-up. Clients with only one assessment are excluded. No minimum gap is enforced; `days_since_initial` is included so a gap rule can be applied downstream.

**Outputs:**

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `cats_self_7_17_paired_clean.csv` | One row per client: initial/follow-up scores, `positive_outcome`, `score_change`, quarter labels, severity bands, cutoff flags, `days_since_initial` |
| `cats_caregiver_7_17_paired_clean.csv` | Same, caregiver report 7–17 |
| `cats_caregiver_3_6_paired_clean.csv` | Same, caregiver report 3–6 (bands: Not clinical / Clinical) |

# Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Reads an eInsight assessment CSV export with two-row headers.
# Row 1 holds question text (merged cells export as blanks and are forward-
# filled); row 2 holds sub-headers ("Response", "Score", ...). Returns a data
# frame with combined snake_case names and fully blank columns removed.
# "0" is deliberately NOT treated as missing: it is a valid rating on most tools.
read_assessment_csv <- function(path, na_vals = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A")) {
  raw <- read_csv(path, na = na_vals, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE,
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

  h1    <- unlist(raw[1, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h2    <- unlist(raw[2, ], use.names = FALSE)
  h1_ff <- na.locf(h1, na.rm = FALSE) |> str_squish()

  new_names <- ifelse(
    is.na(h1_ff) | h1_ff == "",
    h2,
    paste(h1_ff, h2, sep = " - ")
  )
  new_names <- janitor::make_clean_names(new_names)

  df <- raw[-c(1, 2), ]
  names(df) <- new_names

  df |> select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))
}

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Stops if the number of item columns differs from what scoring expects.
# Scoring is positional, so a missing or extra column would silently shift
# reverse-scored items and weights onto the wrong questions.
check_items <- function(cols, expected, label) {
  if (length(cols) != expected) {
    stop(label, ": expected ", expected, " item columns but found ", length(cols), ":\n  ",
         paste(cols, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  message(label, ": found ", expected, " item columns as expected.")
  invisible(cols)
}

# Maps text responses to numbers, ignoring case and extra whitespace
# (e.g., "Strongly Disagree", "strongly disagree " and "Strongly disagree" all match).
map_responses <- function(x, map) {
  keys <- str_to_lower(str_squish(names(map)))
  unname(map[match(str_to_lower(str_squish(x)), keys)])
}

# Lists non-blank responses that do not match the scoring map. These would
# otherwise become NA silently and be counted as missing items.
# Returns the unmatched values (empty table = everything matched).
audit_unmapped <- function(df, cols, map, label) {
  keys <- str_to_lower(str_squish(names(map)))
  bad  <- df |>
    select(all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !str_to_lower(str_squish(value)) %in% keys) |>
    count(value, name = "n_values", sort = TRUE)
  if (nrow(bad) > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", sum(bad$n_values), " non-blank response(s) did not match the scoring map ",
            "and are treated as missing (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all non-blank responses match the scoring map.")
  }
  bad
}

# After reverse scoring, every item should correlate positively with the sum of
# the anchor items (excluding itself). Pass the items the instrument never
# reverse-scores as `anchor`: comparing against all items can hide a block of
# reversed items that mostly agree with each other. A negative value means the
# item's direction is wrong (reversed twice, or a positively worded item that
# was not reversed). Returns only the items that need a look (empty = all fine).
item_rest_check <- function(df, cols, label, anchor = cols) {
  anchor_sum <- rowSums(df[anchor], na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- tibble(
    item        = cols,
    item_rest_r = map_dbl(cols, function(col) {
      rest <- anchor_sum - if (col %in% anchor) coalesce(df[[col]], 0) else 0
      suppressWarnings(cor(df[[col]], rest, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    })
  )
  n_neg <- sum(out$item_rest_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_neg, " item(s) correlate negatively with the rest of the scale; ",
            "check reverse scoring (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item-rest correlations are positive.")
  }
  out |> filter(item_rest_r < 0 | is.na(item_rest_r))
}

# Missing-item policy (decided October 2026, D10): use the instrument's
# published rule where one exists; otherwise allow up to 10% of items to be
# blank and prorate. Filled-in values are rounded half up to whole numbers,
# as the published rules do.
round_half_up <- function(x) floor(x + 0.5)

default_max_missing <- function(n_items) floor(0.10 * n_items)

# Scores a total from a data frame holding only the item columns. Rows with
# more than `max_missing` blank items get NA. Otherwise blanks are filled in
# by `method`:
#   "prorate":   total = sum of answered items x number of items / number answered
#   "item_mean": each blank item takes the rounded mean of the answered items
#   "zero":      blank items count as 0 (the PSC-35 rule)
# When `label` is given, reports how many totals were filled in or set to NA.
score_total <- function(items, max_missing, method = c("prorate", "item_mean", "zero"), label = NULL) {
  method   <- match.arg(method)
  items    <- as.matrix(items)
  answered <- rowSums(!is.na(items))
  n_blank  <- ncol(items) - answered
  item_sum <- rowSums(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  total <- switch(method,
    prorate   = round_half_up(item_sum * ncol(items) / answered),
    item_mean = item_sum + n_blank * round_half_up(item_sum / answered),
    zero      = item_sum
  )
  total[n_blank > max_missing] <- NA_real_
  if (!is.null(label)) {
    message(label, ": ", sum(n_blank > 0 & n_blank <= max_missing), " total(s) with up to ",
            max_missing, " blank item(s) filled in (", method, "); ", sum(n_blank > max_missing),
            " set to NA (more than ", max_missing, " of ", ncol(items), " items blank).")
  }
  total
}

# Finds the item columns answered on a response scale: the "_response" columns
# where at least half of the non-blank answers match `map`. Yes/No and
# free-text questions on the same form drop out. If the count differs from
# `expected`, prints each response column's share of answers on the scale and
# stops (via check_items()).
scale_item_cols <- function(df, map, expected, label) {
  resp  <- names(df)[endsWith(names(df), "_response")]
  share <- map_dbl(resp, ~ mean(!is.na(map_responses(na.omit(df[[.x]]), map))))
  items <- resp[share >= 0.5 & !is.nan(share)]
  if (length(items) != expected) {
    print(tibble(column = resp, share_on_scale = round(share, 2)), n = Inf)
  }
  check_items(items, expected, label)
}
```

```{r}
cats_check <- read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, cats_files[["self_7_17"]]))

item_like <- names(cats_check)[str_detect(names(cats_check), "_(response|score)$") &
                               !str_detect(names(cats_check), "describe|bother")]

tibble(
  column     = item_like,
  n_answered = map_int(item_like, ~ sum(!is.na(cats_check[[.x]]))),
  n_values   = map_int(item_like, ~ n_distinct(cats_check[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE)),
  values     = map_chr(item_like, ~ {
    v <- sort(unique(na.omit(cats_check[[.x]])))
    if (length(v) <= 6 && all(nchar(v) <= 25)) paste(v, collapse = " | ") else "(not shown)"
  })
) |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

## Scoring Parameters

Each version's response scale, the item each symptom row belongs to (in form order), and its published bands, given as the top score of each band.

```{r scoring-params}
scale_7_17 <- c("Never" = 0, "Sometimes" = 1, "Often" = 2, "Almost always" = 3)

cats_7_17 <- list(
  scale       = scale_7_17,
  item_of_row = c(1:8, rep(9, 4), rep(10, 2), 11:14, rep(15, 2), 16:20),
  bands       = c("Normal" = 14, "Moderate" = 20, "Elevated" = 24, "Probable PTSD" = 60),
  cutoff      = 21
)

cats_versions <- list(
  self_7_17      = cats_7_17,
  caregiver_7_17 = cats_7_17,
  caregiver_3_6  = list(
    scale       = c("Never" = 0, "Once in a while" = 1, "Half the time" = 2, "Almost always" = 3),
    item_of_row = 1:16,
    bands       = c("Not clinical" = 11, "Clinical" = 48),
    cutoff      = 12
  )
)
```

## Score and Pair

All three versions share the same steps after their parameters are set.

```{r cats-helper}
score_and_pair_cats <- function(df, version, label) {
  row_cols <- scale_item_cols(df, version$scale, length(version$item_of_row), label)
  print(audit_unmapped(df, row_cols, version$scale, label))

  rows <- df |> mutate(across(all_of(row_cols), ~ map_responses(.x, version$scale)))

  # Split items (9, 10, 15) count their highest answered sub-item
  items <- split.default(rows[row_cols], version$item_of_row) |>
    map(~ do.call(pmax, c(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
    as_tibble(.name_repair = ~ paste0("item_", .x))
  print(item_rest_check(items, names(items), label))

  scored <- bind_cols(rows, items) |>
    mutate(date_completed = parse_einsight_date(date_completed)) |>
    filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date)) |>
    mutate(total_score = score_total(pick(all_of(names(items))), default_max_missing(ncol(items)),
                                     label = label)) |>
    select(client_system_id, collection, date_completed, total_score)

  cat(label, "rows after scoring:  ", nrow(scored), "\n")
  cat(label, "missing total_score: ", sum(is.na(scored$total_score)), "\n")

  severity_band <- function(score) cut(score, breaks = c(-Inf, version$bands), labels = names(version$bands))

  scored |>
    group_by(client_system_id) |>
    arrange(date_completed, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    summarise(
      n_assessments   = n(),
      initial_date    = first(date_completed),
      initial_score   = first(total_score),
      follow_up_date  = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(date_completed), as.Date(NA)),
      follow_up_score = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(total_score),    NA_real_),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(follow_up_date)) |>
    mutate(
      # Lower follow-up = positive outcome: 1 = improved, 0 = no change, -1 = worsened
      positive_outcome       = as.integer(sign(initial_score - follow_up_score)),
      score_change           = follow_up_score - initial_score,
      initial_quarter        = paste0("Q", quarter(initial_date),    " ", year(initial_date)),
      follow_up_quarter      = paste0("Q", quarter(follow_up_date), " ", year(follow_up_date)),
      initial_severity       = severity_band(initial_score),
      follow_up_severity     = severity_band(follow_up_score),
      initial_above_cutoff   = initial_score   >= version$cutoff,
      follow_up_above_cutoff = follow_up_score >= version$cutoff,
      days_since_initial     = as.integer(follow_up_date - initial_date)
    )
}

summarise_cats <- function(paired) {
  paired |>
    summarise(
      n_paired           = n(),
      n_improved         = sum(positive_outcome ==  1, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_no_change        = sum(positive_outcome ==  0, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_worsened         = sum(positive_outcome == -1, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_improved       = round(100 * n_improved / n_paired, 1),
      n_missing_outcome  = sum(is.na(positive_outcome)),
      n_fu_within_3_days = sum(days_since_initial <= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Score and Pair All Versions

```{r cats-run}
cats_paired <- imap(cats_versions, function(version, name) {
  label <- paste("CATS", name)
  read_assessment_csv(file.path(in_dir, cats_files[[name]])) |>
    remove_demo_rows(label) |>
    score_and_pair_cats(version, label)
})

map(cats_paired, nrow)

map(cats_paired, summarise_cats) |> bind_rows(.id = "version")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Write Clean CSVs

```{r write-csvs}
iwalk(cats_paired, ~ write_csv(.x, file.path(out_dir, paste0("cats_", .y, "_paired_clean.csv"))))

cat("CSVs written successfully.\n")
```
